lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p1 - Listen and point

details: Listen and point allows students to practise sound–meaning matching. Pointing confirms accurate identification of the words they hear.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing to Tom, Izzy or Coco and consistent matching of spoken words to the correct character.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p31 - Point and say: say hello!

details: Point & say. Say hello! reinforces recognition of key words by linking each one to a visual prompt. Pointing confirms who is being identified, while saying supports accurate pronunciation and early word associations.
Look for accurate pointing to the correct character, clear saying of names or greeting, and students matching the correct image to its sound confidently.
